SYNTHETIC TEST CASE — entirely invented, no patient identifiers.
A 66-year-old woman with left anterior thigh pain and chronic low back pain.
MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension.
SURGICAL HISTORY
Appendectomy.
CURRENT MEDICATIONS
Amlodipine 5 mg daily.
ALLERGIES
NKDA. No contrast allergy.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives with her spouse. Retired. No tobacco use.
PREVIOUS PAIN MEDICATIONS
Gabapentin — dizziness.
PREVIOUS / CURRENT NON-PHARM
Physiotherapy and home exercises.
INVESTIGATIONS
Lumbar MRI: left L4–5 foraminal narrowing.
PREVIOUS PAIN PROCEDURES
None.
PAIN HISTORY
Left anterior thigh pain worsens with prolonged standing. Home exercises help her back pain.
EXAM
Motor: L2–S1 5/5 bilaterally.
Sensation: L2–S1 intact to light touch bilaterally.
Reflexes: Patellar and Achilles 2+ bilaterally.
IMPRESSION
Possible left L4 radicular pain.
PLAN
Left L4 selective nerve root block.
